correctness.rationale: The sharp longest-chain slab bound and origin witness determine radius; equalities along adjacent-swapped Boolean maximal chains force rank-constant coordinates and zero rank-sum; rank-omission inequalities give the exact coordinate cap. A convexity inequality using selected and complementary ranks proves every remaining chain constraint. Active-bound enumeration proves dimension and parity vertex counts for every integer d≥1. Exact rational rank and exhaustive finite slack tests for d=1..6 corroborate but do not substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The primary Hlavacek thesis and Beck–Hlavacek signed-polytope paper supply objects and combinatorial properties, but not the Euclidean center locus. The already known enriched-chain inradius can imply the same numeric radius but not this distinct body's positive-dimensional full incenter set, as shown explicitly by the two-element-chain discrepancy. Targeted equivalence, stronger-theorem, and tabulation comparisons were made; residual publication search incompleteness remains.

value.rationale: The Boolean inclusion poset is a canonical, parameter-free family with 2^d ambient coordinates. The result exactly determines all optimal inscribed-ball centers, their surprising affine dimension d, a concrete cube-section model and a parity-sharp vertex count. It distinguishes Euclidean geometry of signed versus absolute-sum and ordinary chain constructions. This is a natural complete geometric classification, not merely an inradius re-evaluation or arbitrary low-order enumeration.
